## Principles

Source: guidelines/principles.md

These principles decide the cases the other guidelines do not cover. When two rules seem to conflict, the earlier principle wins.

1. **Clinical clarity.** Sober and high-contrast. Nothing is decorative unless it carries meaning: colour communicates a role, a state or an emphasis, never an ornament. Every coloured element must earn its place.
2. **One accent.** Navy (`--mq-accent`, `#0a2463`) is the only brand accent, on every surface (ADR-0003). Everything else is a warm neutral or the blue-grey family. Interactive apps add status colours for genuine system status only (ADR-0004).
3. **The figure before the adjective.** A claim is backed by a number, and every number can be traced to its source. Figures are the hero of a page: they get the largest type, the accent colour and room around them. Any fictitious figure says so on the page.
4. **Calm confidence.** Pale neutral surfaces, generous whitespace, one idea per block and one hero figure per column. When a page is full, cut content before shrinking text.
5. **Document-grade.** Every document reads as well printed on A4 or exported to PDF as on a screen. A design that only works on a screen is not finished.
6. **Sober motion, never required.** Motion is optional, short and carries meaning (a bar grows, a line draws). Nothing loops, and print always shows the final state.
7. **Three families, three roles.** Outfit for headings, labels and app UI; Newsreader for reading text; Geist Mono for codes, table figures and dates (typography).
8. **One system, many media.** Slides, A4 reports, papers, the website, newsletters and apps share the same tokens. Media differ in what they may use (documents never carry status colours), never in the values themselves.

## The medium split

Source: guidelines/colour.md

| Medium | Colours allowed | How a state is shown |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Documents: slides, A4 reports, papers, newsletters, the website | Navy, the neutrals, the blue-grey family, the chart tokens | By mark style: solid, ring, pale, outline, quiet, dashed, struck through |
| Interactive apps | Everything documents use, plus `--mq-success`, `--mq-warning`, `--mq-danger`, `--mq-info` | Status colour for genuine system status only (errors, validation, alerts, confirmations), always with an icon or a word |

Documents never carry green, orange, red, sky blue, pink, purple or turquoise, not even to say good or bad (ADR-0004). They never load `css/app.css`. A callout in a document is always navy; there is no warning-orange or success-green callout.

## Accent

Source: guidelines/colour.md

| Token | Value | Use |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--mq-accent` | `#0a2463` | The single accent: key figures, links, active states, the key column of a table, top and edge rules, series 1, navy panels |
| `--mq-accent-hover` | `#061a4d` | Hover and pressed state of a link or an accent control, nothing else |
| `--mq-accent-pale` | `#eaeef7` | Icon pills and chips, a deviating value, the highlighted table row, the pale state |
| `--mq-accent-pale-2` | `#f2f4f9` | Progress tracks, the quiet state, callout background |
| `--mq-on-accent` | `#ffffff` | Text and icons on an accent fill (14.53:1) |

Navy carries emphasis on its own. Status colours never replace it for emphasis, in any medium.

## Neutrals

Source: guidelines/colour.md

The neutrals are warm greys tuned to the warm canvas, never blue-tinted greys.

| Token | Value | Use | Contrast |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--mq-ink` | `#1a1a1a` | Primary text and values | 16.65:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-muted` | `#555555` | Secondary text, leads, captions | 7.13:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-tertiary` | `#707070` | Tertiary text: notes, footers, axis labels, placeholders (owner ruling 1) | 4.74:1 on canvas, 4.95:1 on surface |
| `--mq-decoration` | `#8c8c8c` | Non-text decoration only: axis lines, ticks, an icon beside its label. Never text (owner ruling 1) | 3.22:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-canvas` | `#fafaf8` | Background of every document page: A4 report, paper, slide (owner ruling 9) | |
| `--mq-surface` | `#ffffff` | Cards, panels, tables, figures, inputs | |
| `--mq-surface-alt` | `#f5f4f1` | Recessed areas: table headers, tab bars, grouped areas, hover | |
| `--mq-desk` | `#e9e8e4` | On screen only, around a page preview; never inside a document, so a printed page is never grey (owner ruling 9) | |
| `--mq-border` | `#dddbd6` | Borders, dividers, chart baselines | decorative |
| `--mq-border-light` | `#ebeae6` | Hairlines between rows and columns, card borders | decorative |
| `--mq-border-strong` | `#5d6f91` | Outline of outlined and dashed state marks | 4.84:1 on canvas, non-text |

Why a warm canvas: pure white reads clinical and generic; the warm off-white reads institutional while white cards still stand out on it. Tertiary text sits exactly at 4.50:1 on `--mq-surface-alt`, so put it on canvas or surface, not on the recessed grey.

## Status colours (apps only)

Source: guidelines/colour.md

| Token | Value | Use | Contrast |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--mq-success` | `#2e7d32` | Confirmation, published, valid | 5.13:1 on surface, 4.91:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-danger` | `#d8232a` | Errors, destructive actions | 5.01:1 on surface, 4.79:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-info` | `#1565c0` | Information | 5.75:1 on surface, 5.50:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-warning` | `#a06400` | Warning text, icons and borders | 4.86:1 on surface, 4.65:1 on canvas |
| `--mq-warning-fill` | `#d4850a` | Warning badge or highlight fill, always with ink text (5.93:1) | Fill only |
| `--mq-warning-tint` | `#fbf3e7` | Warning background behind ink text (15.81:1) | Fill only |

The warning split (owner ruling 5): the orange `#d4850a` is a fill and never text, an icon or a border (2.81:1 on canvas). Text on it is ink; white on it is forbidden (2.93:1). On the warning tint, the text stays ink and `--mq-warning` is used only for the icon and the border (4.42:1, non-text).

Every status colour comes with an icon or a word (WCAG 1.4.1):

- a status badge carries its word, an urgent flag adds an icon and a border (`mq-status` in `css/app.css`);
- a status column shows a small coloured dot followed by the plain word, not a badge;
- a flag is a coloured word, and only on the rows that need attention, so normal rows stay quiet;
- light badge backgrounds come from the 50 and 100 steps of the status scales in `dist/tailwind.css`, never a hand-picked tint.

The red of the old Paracel theme survives only as `--mq-danger` (ADR-0003). App-specific hues, such as the annotation colours of regulatory text, stay local in the app under its own prefix until a second consumer needs them (specialising).

## Three families, three roles

Source: guidelines/typography.md

| Family | Token | Role |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Outfit | `--mq-font-family-heading`, `--mq-font-family-ui` | Headings, column titles, hero figures, labels, table text, takeaways; the whole UI of apps (navigation, buttons, badges, UI body text) |
| Newsreader | `--mq-font-family-body` | Reading text: body of documents and slides, leads, captions, notes, quoted official text, and regulatory text in apps. The only serif (owner ruling 10) |
| Geist Mono | `--mq-font-family-mono` | Codes, figures in tables, dates in tables, eyebrows, axis labels, identifiers |

Georgia and Times New Roman appear only as fallbacks. The three families are self-hosted (`fonts/fonts.css`, variable woff2 with latin and latin-ext); no page loads a font from a remote service. Newsreader ships its true italic, so leads and notes are never a slanted roman.

Outfit was chosen because it reads cleanly from a display title down to an 11 px badge, with a geometric, contemporary character that stays distinct from the generic interface sans-serifs.

## Weights

Source: guidelines/typography.md

| Weight | Token | Use |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Outfit 500 | `--mq-font-weight-heading` | Every heading, column title, hero figure, KPI value, label, button label and badge (owner ruling 4) |
| Outfit 600 | `--mq-font-weight-emphasis` | Only a short highlighted word inside body text, as the "Med" of the wordmark. Bold inside Newsreader prose switches to Outfit 600 at about 0.94 em |
| Outfit 400 | `--mq-font-weight-body` | App UI body text |
| Outfit 300 | | Only the "Quantis" half of the wordmark |
| Newsreader 400 | `--mq-font-weight-body` | Reading text, with its italic for leads and notes |
| Geist Mono 400 and 500 | | Table figures and codes 400, eyebrows 500 |

Weights 700 and 800 appear only inside the monogram files; no heading, button or table uses them.

## Line height

Source: guidelines/typography.md

| Context | Line height |
| :-- | :-- |
| Hero titles | 1.04 to 1.08 |
| Headings, counters, stat figures | 1.15 to 1.3 |
| Leads | 1.5 |
| App UI text, labels, descriptions | 1.55 |
| Reading text in documents | 1.6 |
| Help text and longer descriptions in apps | 1.75 |
| Regulatory text in apps (dense legal prose read under time pressure) | 2.2, and 2.0 on phones |

Long regulatory text is set in Newsreader at about 15 px with that generous line height, so long German compounds stay separable line by line. Codes inside it are set in Geist Mono at 12 px on the recessed surface with the small radius. Dense tables keep tight padding; the breathing room goes to the text people read word by word.

## App type scale

Source: guidelines/typography.md

Apps use the same families and weights at UI sizes: UI body Outfit 400 at 14 px, help text 13 to 14 px at line height 1.75, labels and navigation Outfit 500 at 13 px, badges Outfit 500 at 11 px, data values Geist Mono at 12 to 13 px, page title Outfit 500. Heavier weights (600 to 800) and sizes below 11 px from older app designs are retired.

## Radius

Source: guidelines/layout.md

Owner ruling 3, as amended on 2026-10-10:

| Token | Value | For |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--mq-radius-small` | 3 px | Small items: tags, chips, badges, inputs, buttons, progress tracks, bar ends, tooltips |
| `--mq-radius-medium` | 6 px | Cards, panels, KPI tiles, figures, icon pills, slide frames. The maximum anywhere else |
| `--mq-radius-overlay` | 12 px | Apps only: dialogs and modals, side drawers and command palettes. Never in documents, slides, cards or website media |

- No pill shapes, ever: no fully rounded buttons, tags, chips or tabs.
- A circle is allowed only for something that is genuinely round: a status dot, a numbered marker, an avatar. In Tailwind that is `rounded-full`, and only there.
- In `dist/tailwind.css` the steps `rounded`, `rounded-xs` and `rounded-sm` resolve to 3 px, `rounded-md` to `rounded-4xl` to 6 px, and `rounded-overlay` to 12 px, so no utility class can exceed the ruling. The shared stylelint config rejects any other radius.

Squared-off corners read professional and institutional; pills read consumer.

## Elevation and navy blocks

Source: guidelines/layout.md

- Cards, figures and tables: `--mq-shadow-small`. Raised panels, menus and a page or slide previewed on the desk: `--mq-shadow-medium`. Navy panels: `--mq-shadow-panel`. No shadow in print and none on chart marks.
- One large navy block per screen, slide or page area. In a report, keep the header, a navy KPI band and a navy panel apart with light content.

## Tables

Source: guidelines/layout.md

Document tables (`mq-table`):

- Horizontal hairlines only, never vertical rules and never zebra stripes.
- Headers in Geist Mono capitals on the recessed surface; the unit goes on a second header line ("Gap" then "CHF"), never repeated in every cell.
- Figures in Geist Mono, right-aligned (`mq-num`); the first column in Outfit 500 or Newsreader.
- The key column in navy (`is-key`).
- A deviating value may sit in a pale navy pill with the small radius.
- At most one highlighted row (`tr.is-highlight`): a pale navy fill. The source pattern adds a 3 px navy edge on its first cell; the shared class does not draw it yet.
- An excluded row is struck through in blue-grey 2 and left out of the total (pattern, not yet a class).
- The total row (`tr.is-total`) sits under a 2 px navy rule; its key amount is navy.

App tables (sober tables):

- A white wrapper with a light border, the small shadow and the 6 px radius; recessed header row; row hover on the recessed surface.
- Below a minimum width (about 640 px) the table scrolls horizontally inside its wrapper, never the page.
- Do not put a badge in every column. Use three levels of visual weight so the eye rests on normal rows: small classification marks explained by a legend row under the table, a status dot followed by its word, and flags as coloured words only on the rows that need attention (colour).

## App patterns

Source: guidelines/layout.md

- **Navigation:** links in muted Outfit 500; hover in ink on the recessed surface; the active link in navy on pale navy. On tablets the navigation collapses into a menu.
- **Tabs:** underline tabs, not segmented pills. The active tab is navy with a 2 px navy underline (`--mq-stroke-strong`); hover in ink on the recessed surface. Underline tabs stay light in dense tools.
- **Breadcrumb:** inside a light bordered card; links muted, navy on hover; the separator is a single right angle quote in tertiary; the current page in ink.
- **Buttons:** primary (navy fill, white text, darker navy on hover), secondary (white, border, recessed on hover), danger outline (danger border and text, with an icon or a destructive verb), ghost (no border, muted text). One size, Outfit 500, the small radius. On phones a button row stretches to full width.
- **Empty state:** centred, a dimmed icon, an Outfit 500 title, one muted sentence, and a hint in Geist Mono tertiary.
- **Stat cards:** stable. No hover lift, no animation: reference data must not move under the pointer.
- **Breakpoints:** documents switch to one column below 720 px. Apps use 768 px (tablet: navigation menu, narrower gutters) and 480 px (phone: full-width buttons, two stat cards per row, keys of key-value rows above their values).

## Phones

Source: guidelines/layout.md

One column, a 16 px gutter, and no horizontal scrolling of the page. Only tables and wide charts scroll, inside their own frame.

## No em dash, no en dash

Source: guidelines/writing.md

Never use the em dash or the en dash, in any language, in any copy: slides, reports, pages, emails, app strings, translations and these guidelines. A guideline test fails on either character in `guidelines/`.

Choose the punctuation that matches how the two parts relate:

- a second clause with its own subject becomes a new sentence;
- an aside goes between commas or in parentheses;
- a definition, an explanation or a list lead-in takes a colon;
- two balanced independent clauses take a semicolon;
- a short label pairing (a section number and its name, a scope and its period) takes a middle dot: "04 · Analytics".

A spaced hyphen used as an aside is a disguised dash and follows the same rule. Hyphens inside compound words stay ("Swiss-hosted", "nDSG-konform"). The middle dot and the arrow (→) are allowed.

When translating, never carry a dash over from the source language: restructure the sentence in the target language.

## Titles

Source: guidelines/writing.md

- Sentence case: capital on the first word and on proper nouns only.
- No full stop at the end of a title, even a title of two sentences (drop only the final one).
- Eyebrows and section labels are typed in normal case; CSS sets them in capitals (typography).

## Monogram and favicon

Source: guidelines/brand.md

Where the wordmark does not fit (favicon, app icon, avatar, app tile), use the monogram: a white M and Q on a navy (`#0a2463`) square with rounded corners of 8/64 of its side, M in Outfit 700 and Q in Outfit 400, centred on the cap height (owner ruling 7). The letters are outlined in every file.

| File | Use |
| :-- | :-- |
| `brand/monogram.svg` | The monogram with its rounded corners |
| `brand/monogram-square.svg` | For platforms that round icons themselves |
| `brand/monogram-small.svg` | 16 px and smaller: larger letters, M 800 and Q 600 |
| `brand/favicon/` | `favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico` (16, 32, 48), `apple-touch-icon.png` (180), `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png` |

## Icons

Source: guidelines/brand.md

- Lucide only, from the pinned build in `icons/` (version and hash in `icons/manifest.json`). No second icon library, and never an emoji in place of an icon.
- Icons are offline: the pinned build or an inline SVG, never a CDN or any remote request.
- Monochrome, stroke 2, round caps and joins, colour inherited from the text. Navy on a pale navy pill (`--mq-accent-pale`), white on a navy panel inside a translucent pill (`--mq-on-navy-pill`), blue-grey (`--mq-border-strong`) in a card title bar.
- The icon pill is a small square with the 6 px radius (`--mq-radius-medium`), never a circle or a pill shape.
- An icon that carries meaning has a text label or an accessible name; a decorative icon is hidden from assistive technology.

## Numbers (owner ruling 8, as amended on 2026-10-10)

Source: guidelines/data-patterns.md

| Case | Write | Never |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Thousands | `2'460'000`: the straight apostrophe (U+0027) | the curly apostrophe, a space, a comma, a full stop |
| Decimals | `12.5`: a decimal point, in every language | a decimal comma |
| Percentage | `12.5 %`: a non-breaking space before `%`, in every language | `12.5%`, a breaking space |
| Amount | `CHF 2'460'000`: the currency first, joined to the amount by a non-breaking space | `2'460'000 CHF`, `Fr.`, a breaking space |
| Cents | `CHF 6'826.20`; in a report, round to the franc whenever the cents add nothing | |
| Millions | `CHF 1.2 mio` (French), `CHF 1.2 Mio.` (German), `CHF 1.2 M` (English); in a sentence the word may be written out | a decimal comma |
| Negative | `−150'000`: the minus sign U+2212 | a hyphen |
| Change | `+14 %`, `−3 %`: the sign is enough | a colour or an arrow to show direction |
| Approximation | `~84`, `≈178`: approximate figures stay approximate | false precision |

The Italian abbreviation for millions is not yet defined; the owner is to provide it.

- One number format per document. Never mix two thousands separators, even when quoting a source that uses another one.
- A hero figure stays short, about seven to nine characters. The unit goes in its caption ("CHF of net gap"), not in the figure.
- A table's unit goes in its header, not in every cell (layout).
- Shares of a whole are rounded with the largest-remainder method, so the displayed percentages add up to exactly 100.
- In code, format through one function per pattern (amount, number, percentage) rather than by hand; the specimen script exports such functions.

## Dates and periods

Source: guidelines/data-patterns.md

| Case | Write |
| :-- | :-- |
| Date | `08.10.2026`: day, month, year with full stops |
| Month (axes, tables) | `10.2026` |
| Year (axes) | `2024` |
| Period | `2019 → 2025`, with the arrow |
| Range | `2019-2025` with a plain hyphen, or in words: "3 to 6", « 3 à 6 » |

Never an en dash in a range.

## Null versus zero

Source: guidelines/data-patterns.md

A zero is a measurement; a missing value is not. Keep them apart everywhere:

- **Zero** is written `0` (or `CHF 0`) when the value was measured and is zero.
- **Missing** (not measured, not applicable, not yet available) is never written as `0` and never left as an empty cell. Write the language's "not available" abbreviation: `n.d.` (French and Italian), `k.A.` (German), `n/a` (English), and explain it once in a note under the table or chart.
- A dash is not used for a missing value: it reads as a minus sign or a range.
- An aggregate over values that are all missing is itself missing, never a total of `0`.
- A chart leaves a gap for a missing point; it never draws it at zero.

## Confidential values

Source: guidelines/data-patterns.md

A confidential rate, price, refund scale or commercial term is never invented and never shown, not even as an example. Show a mask instead: a lock icon followed by `••••` in Geist Mono, navy.

## Target

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

WCAG 2.2 level AA for every medium: apps, the website, HTML reports, slides exported to PDF and newsletters. APCA is not normative and is not used; contrast is measured with the WCAG 2.x formula.

## Colour is never alone

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

Colour never carries meaning on its own (WCAG 1.4.1):

- documents show states by mark style (solid, ring, pale, outline, quiet, dashed, struck through) and a page that uses these marks gives their key once, in a legend or a note;
- apps pair every status colour with an icon or a word;
- charts label the marks that use series 3 or 4, or give them an outline, since those colours are below 3:1 on the page (charts);
- a change in a figure is shown by its sign, not by a colour or an arrow alone.

## Contrast pairs

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

Every foreground and background pair the system uses is declared in `tokens/contrast-pairs.json` with its allowed use: text (4.5:1), large text (3:1), non-text (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11) or decorative (no minimum, for marks that carry no information). The token test checks every declared pair and fails on any pairing used in `css/` without a declaration; the specimen shows each pair with its ratio. A consumer that needs a new pair asks for it here rather than eyeballing it.

Pairs to remember:

| Pair | Ratio | Allowed for |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Ink on canvas | 16.65:1 | Text |
| Muted on canvas | 7.13:1 | Text |
| Tertiary on canvas, on surface | 4.74:1, 4.95:1 | Text. Not on the recessed surface (exactly 4.50:1, not declared) |
| Decoration grey on canvas | 3.22:1 | Non-text only, never text |
| Navy on canvas | 13.90:1 | Text |
| White on navy | 14.53:1 | Text |
| On-navy accent on the lighter panel stop | 4.61:1 | Text, narrow margin |
| On-navy discreet (white at 40 %) on navy | 3.48:1 | Large text or non-text only |
| Warning text on surface | 4.86:1 | Text |
| Ink on the warning fill | 5.93:1 | Text; white on the fill is forbidden (2.93:1) |
| Blue-grey outline on canvas | 4.84:1 | Non-text |

Placeholder text in inputs uses the tertiary text colour, never a lighter grey.

## Focus

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

- Every interactive element shows a visible focus ring on keyboard focus (WCAG 2.4.7 and 1.4.11): `--mq-focus-ring-width` (2 px) of `--mq-focus-ring-color` (navy, 13.90:1 on canvas) at `--mq-focus-ring-offset` (2 px) from the element.
- On navy, the ring is white (`--mq-focus-ring-color-on-navy`, 14.53:1). `css/base.css` and `css/components.css` draw both.
- Never remove the outline without drawing this ring. A focused input may also change its border to navy, but the ring stays.

## Size and targets

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

- No text below 11 px on screen (typography).
- Touch targets in apps are at least 44 px high on mobile (buttons, tabs, navigation links), above the 24 px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8.
- Text reflows: pages work at 320 px wide and at 200 % zoom without horizontal page scrolling; only tables and wide charts scroll inside their frame.

## Motion

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

- Motion is optional, short and meaningful. Interactive elements may use short transitions (about 120 ms) on colour and background; documents do not animate on hover.
- Never blur, zoom, reflections, spotlight effects or looping animation.
- Everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (no animation at all) and print shows the final state.

## Structure

Source: guidelines/accessibility.md

- One `h1` per page and headings in order; the eyebrow is not a heading.
- Set the page language (`lang`) and mark passages in another language.
- An SVG chart has `role="img"` and an accessible name and description (`<title>` and `<desc>`, or `aria-labelledby`); the figure's key values also appear in text or in a table.
- Icons that carry meaning have a label; decorative icons are hidden (`aria-hidden="true"`).
- PDFs exported from HTML are tagged and carry an outline (Playwright `tagged` and `outline`); the specimen test exports one.

## Framework neutrality

Source: guidelines/specialising.md

The design system ships framework-neutral outputs only: CSS custom properties (`dist/tokens.css`), resolved values (`dist/tokens.json`), a Tailwind theme (`dist/tailwind.css`), the kit contract for kit renderers (`dist/kit-contract.css`), the shared `mq-` CSS, fonts, icons and brand files. It ships no framework component.

- Wiring the tokens into a component library (Nuxt UI, shadcn/ui, Radix, MUI) belongs to the consumer. For example, a component library that names its error colour `error` maps it to `--mq-danger` in the app, not here.
- When two consumers need the same wiring, it may ship here as a separate optional export generated from the tokens, never as part of the core outputs.
- Apps with a component library take the tokens and the Tailwind theme only. They do not load the `mq-` component CSS and never load `kit-contract.css`, whose unprefixed names collide with framework variables.

## Use what exists first

Source: guidelines/specialising.md

- Build documents from the shared `mq-` classes with their documented markup. Every shared class carries the `mq-` prefix so it never collides with a consumer's classes.
- Add no colour, font, shadow, radius or spacing that is not a token. When a need is not covered, combine existing components before inventing one.
- The specimen (`make specimen`, then `dist/specimen/index.html`) is the visual reference; when a rendering is in doubt, it decides.
- Pin an exact release; never a range or a branch.

## The four rules

Source: guidelines/specialising.md

1. **Core and semantic tokens are never overridden in a consumer.** A consumer does not redefine `--mq-accent` or any other `--mq-*` name.
2. **A product-level variation is a theme in this repository**, never a local override. There is no theme in v1 (ADR-0003).
3. **Local additions use the consumer's own prefix** (`--deck-*`, `--app-*`) and reference `var(--mq-*)` only. The shared stylelint config (`@medquantis/design-system/stylelint`) rejects literal colours, fonts and shadows, `!important`, unknown custom properties and any radius other than the three radius tokens. A repository whose dense views need a sans body may override its own body family locally under its prefix.
4. **A component invented locally in two consumers is a candidate for promotion** into this repository.

## Colour tokens for this medium

Generated from dist/tokens.json. Sizes, spacing, radii and fonts: run `python3 scripts/tokens.py`.

| Token | Value | Use |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `--mq-chart-series-1` | `#0a2463` | Categorical series 1 of 4, always used first; also the highlight in highlight-on-grey charts. |
